paragraphs: Virtual Peaker sells cloud software that lets an electric utility reach the smart devices already sitting in homes and businesses and use them to shave peak load and cost. The buyers are utilities standing up demand response programs.

Three suites make up the product, and the company presents them together as a virtual power plant platform that aggregates distributed energy resources at the edge of the grid. The Shift suite is the dispatch side, aggregating resources at homes and at commercial and industrial sites to hold down peak market costs and defer new construction. The Relay suite handles the customer side, signing people up and paying out the incentives. A utility can run several program types at once across electric vehicles, thermostats, water heaters and batteries.

The company describes partnerships with more than thirty device types, from thermostats to electric vehicle chargers. It states that the platform is SOC 2 Type 2 certified. Municipal energy providers are named as one audience, using demand response to meet grid goals and engage customers. One published case study covers Sacramento Municipal Utility District optimizing hot water heater efficiency on the platform.

quote.text: Modern utilities use Virtual Peaker to launch demand response programs.
